To: Engineering Leadership  
From: Infrastructure / AI Platform  
Re: Local AI hardware vs hosted models  

Recommendation: do not make local AI hardware the default path for our workloads. Hosted models should remain the primary option for most product and internal-tool use because they deliver faster iteration, elastic capacity, strong model access, and lower operational burden. Buying GPUs creates a fixed asset problem: procurement lead time, rack/power/cooling constraints, driver and runtime maintenance, security patching, utilization risk, and a small team accountable for availability. For variable or bursty workloads, that fixed capacity is often underused, which pushes total cost upward even if per-token pricing looks higher at first glance.

Local hardware makes sense only where constraints are explicit: strict data-residency requirements, regulated work

Recommendation: do not make a broad local-hardware purchase as the default path for our AI workloads. Use hosted models for general product, internal tooling, and most experimentation, while reserving on-prem or dedicated hardware for a small set of explicitly justified cases such as strict data-residency requirements, latency-sensitive edge workflows, or sustained very high utilization where the math clearly favors ownership.

To: Engineering leadership
From: Platform/Infrastructure
Re: Local AI hardware vs hosted models

Recommendation: do not standardize on buying local AI hardware as the default path for our workloads. Hosted models should remain the primary option for most product and internal-tool use because they reduce up-front capital spend, shorten time to production, and shift model maintenance, scaling, and reliability to vendors whose core business is exactly that. For a team without a dedicated ML operations group, owning GPUs introduces a long tail of work: procurement, rack/power planning, driver and container compatibility, monitoring, failover, patching, capacity forecasting, and disposal. Those costs are easy to underestimate and are rarely recovered just because inference appears “cheaper” on a per-token spreadsheet.
